questions.title: Why did the D.C. Circuit raise Article III standing sua sponte after the district court already ruled on the merits?
questions.question_body: I'm confused about the procedural posture here. The district court dismissed AFL's claims on the merits (failure to state a claim), and neither party initially briefed standing in the appeal. Yet, the appellate court ordered supplemental briefing on standing and ultimately vacated the judgment for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction. Under what circumstances can an appellate court ignore the merits and decide standing on its own? Does *Steel Co.* require this even if the lower court already spent resources deciding the case?

questions.title: How does the 'relaxed' standing test for procedural injuries differ from standard standing, and why did AFL still fail?
questions.question_body: The opinion mentions that when a plaintiff alleges a violation of a procedural right designed to protect a concrete interest, courts 'relax' the requirements for imminence and redressability. However, the court says AFL failed even this relaxed standard. What exactly is the difference between proving injury/causation under the standard *Lujan* test versus this 'procedural injury' framework? Specifically, why wasn't the statutory mandate that OSC 'shall... conduct an investigation' enough to satisfy the injury element?

questions.title: Why was the causal chain between OSC's inaction and DOJ's withholding considered too 'speculative' to support standing?
questions.question_body: AFL argued that if OSC had investigated, they might have sanctioned DOJ employees, which might have compelled DOJ to release the records. The court rejected this as too attenuated because it relies on the choices of independent actors (MSPB and DOJ). How does this application of *Heckler v. Chaney* (agency discretion) and *FDA v. Alliance for Hippocratic Medicine* (independent actors) work in practice? At what point does a 'likely' outcome become mere 'speculation' in a FOIA enforcement context?

questions.title: What distinguishes an 'informational injury' based on a statutory entitlement from a mere hope of receiving information during an investigation?
questions.question_body: The court rejects AFL's second theory: that they were injured by not getting updates/notices from OSC. The opinion states that informational standing requires being denied information a statute 'entitled him to receive.' Since § 1216 mandates an investigation but doesn't explicitly mandate notice to the complainant (unlike § 1214), AFL had no entitlement. Is there any scenario where a plaintiff has standing to force an agency to investigate something just to get status updates, or must the underlying statute explicitly create a right to that specific information?

questions.title: Does 5 U.S.C. § 1216(a)(3) create a private right of action for citizens to compel OSC investigations into FOIA violations?
questions.question_body: The text says OSC 'shall... conduct an investigation' of arbitrary FOIA withholdings. Usually, mandatory language like 'shall' implies a duty. However, the court implies that even if this duty exists, a private citizen can't sue to enforce it without standing. If AFL lacks standing because they can't show redressability, does that mean no private citizen ever has standing to enforce § 1216(a)(3)? Is this effectively a commitment of enforcement discretion entirely to OSC, similar to prosecutorial discretion?

questions.title: Why didn't the existence of a separate FOIA lawsuit against DOJ cure the causation problem regarding OSC's failure to act?
questions.question_body: The facts note that AFL already sued DOJ directly under FOIA and is receiving records. AFL tried to argue that OSC's failure to investigate caused them harm because DOJ hadn't produced everything yet. Why couldn't AFL argue that the OSC investigation was a necessary parallel track to ensure full compliance or prevent future violations? Does the fact that DOJ is already producing records undermine any claim of 'imminent' injury required for standing against OSC?
